inv.label: For micro-investors & angels
inv.title: Introduction with prospects
inv.sub: Short narrative. Approximate market context. Sources named. Not a prospectus.
inv.disclaimer: Disclaimer. Figures below are approximate third-party industry estimates for adjacent markets — not AIMarket revenue, ARR, or a promise of capture. Methodologies differ across firms (sometimes by an order of magnitude). Treat as orientation for the room; verify primary reports before diligence. This page is not an offer to sell securities.
inv.h2: Verifiable provenance → agent economy → vertical products
inv.p1: The system preserves who produced a result, from which source, under which checks. Agents can buy one capability call; payment eligibility follows the declared verification policy.
inv.p2: We already ship GAIA (attested IoT), Pay-on-Verified, ATLAS (LIVE vs SIM), Hub, oracles, and operator glass — live URLs above. Capital accelerates volume on those rails and thin entry products (wedges) into verticals that already spend on physical-world data.
inv.pdoor: Incumbents sell forecasts and dashboards. Gaps we productize: per-reading attestation, agent-native micro-billing, economic end for bad data (refund / silence), and honest LIVE vs SIM for humans.
inv.r2b: Visibility software ~low–mid $B; broader SCM tens of $B
inv.r3b: Large fragmented (intensity, DR, metering) — treat as $10B+ opportunity class
inv.r4b: Broad GRC/ESG tooling often cited in tens of $B
inv.tamNote: These are input markets apps plug into — not our booked ARR.
inv.src1: Parametric insurance growth commentary citing Global Market Insights / Allied Market Research / Market.US ranges — Society of Actuaries overview: SOA (Jan 2026). Note: SOA authors stress veracity of marketing-research projections varies.
inv.src2: Parametric market sizing examples: Mordor Intelligence (different definition → much smaller $B) vs broader premium narratives — use the spread as a caution.
inv.src3: Supply chain visibility software: Future Market Insights (~$3.5B in 2026 → ~$12B by 2036 class).
inv.src4: Broader supply chain management: Grand View Research (SCM ~$26B in 2024 → ~$49B by 2030 class).
inv.src5: Live product surfaces (primary, not TAM): GAIA · ATLAS · Hub.
inv.pbuy: Category ownership of agent-native physical oracle + settlement — with a map into insurance, supply chain, energy, compliance, and insight agents. We do not need to be the insurer on day one.
inv.pdata: Diligence starts from the live rails and named sources on this page — not an offline pack.

idea.weather-risk.title: Weather Risk Analyst
idea.weather-risk.teaser: Buy a $0.001 reading. Sell a versioned risk report with a receipt.
idea.weather-risk.lead: Rails are live today — buy weather, verify on GAIA, see LIVE on ATLAS. The risk-report product layer is what you build on top.
idea.weather-risk.artifact: Artifact: versioned risk report (score + drivers) + attestation receipt.
idea.weather-risk.not: Not: insurance payouts or a certified forecast service.
idea.weather-risk.hard: Hard bit: LIVE coverage or explicit degrade/refuse — never silent SIM dressed as LIVE. Touch the live path below first — nothing offline to request.
idea.fire-hotspot.title: Fire + Weather Evidence Snapshot
idea.fire-hotspot.teaser: Buy atlas.fire.weather@v1 — cited FIRMS and/or Copernicus EFFIS plus nearby weather within an explicit distance bound.
idea.fire-hotspot.lead: The callable ATLAS SKU returns NASA FIRMS thermal-anomaly detections and/or Copernicus EFFIS current-fire polygons (listed separately, dual attribution), bounded nearby LIVE weather, limitations, and a content receipt. It is evidence context — not a forecast, perimeter, or risk score. Refuse only if neither LIVE fire class is present. Emberline is an independent desk that buys this SKU.
idea.fire-hotspot.who: Who pays: utilities, land operations, and risk desks that need source-attributed situational evidence.
idea.fire-hotspot.artifact: Artifact: FIRMS hotspots[] and/or EFFIS polygons + bounded weather context + limitations + content receipt.
idea.fire-hotspot.not: Not: a confirmed fire perimeter, forecast, risk rating, evacuation order, dispatch, or insurance decision.
idea.fire-hotspot.hard: Hard bit: keep FIRMS and EFFIS as two products; preserve observation provenance; refuse when both are empty; never attach distant weather or pad with SIM.
idea.fire-hotspot.step3: Discover the paid invoke on Hub
idea.verified-watchbox.title: ATLAS Verified Watchbox
idea.verified-watchbox.teaser: One bbox + layers → current matches, explicit LIVE/SIM modes, and a content receipt.
idea.verified-watchbox.lead: atlas.watchbox.check@v1 is callable today. It evaluates a saved or ephemeral geographic watchbox against the current ATLAS fleet snapshot and returns source-attributed matches without pretending that empty space equals coverage. Emberline is an independent desk that buys this SKU.
idea.verified-watchbox.who: Who pays: monitoring agents, site operations, and logistics workflows that repeatedly poll a defined area.
idea.verified-watchbox.artifact: Artifact: evaluated bbox, layer set, matches[], LIVE count, evaluation time, and content receipt.
idea.verified-watchbox.not: Not: a push notification, prediction, guaranteed coverage, or proof that an unobserved event did not happen.
idea.verified-watchbox.hard: Hard bit: turn polling into a buyer workflow with deduplication, change detection, and delivery policy while preserving sparse-coverage semantics.
idea.emberline-desk.title: Emberline Fire Evidence Desk
idea.emberline-desk.teaser: Independent desk that buys atlas.watchbox.check@v1 and atlas.fire.weather@v1 — a signed brief, not a perimeter.
idea.emberline-desk.lead: Emberline is a third-party Fire Evidence Desk. It is not an AIMarket brand surface and not a clone of the Fire Glass product page. The desk polls a saved bbox, buys the callable ATLAS SKUs, and files a signed brief. Open the sample, then the desk — this catalog card does not invoke Hub.
idea.emberline-desk.who: Who pays: land ops and utilities that need a signed evidence brief, not another map to watch.
idea.emberline-desk.artifact: Artifact: signed fire-evidence brief (watchbox matches + fire/weather snapshot + limitations) and a shareable desk link.
idea.emberline-desk.not: Not: a confirmed perimeter, forecast, dispatch, insurance decision, or a first-party AIMarket product.
idea.emberline-desk.hard: Hard bit: keep FIRMS and EFFIS as two products; refuse empty coverage honestly; never dress SIM as LIVE. This card is an example consumer of the SKUs — fork the desk pattern; do not pay from USE.
idea.emberline-desk.step3: Inspect the fire+weather SKU this desk buys
idea.situation-brief.title: Situation Brief (ATLAS > parts)
idea.situation-brief.teaser: One bbox → multi-layer scored brief with LIVE citations. Defaults to map layers including flood, EFFIS, lightning, volcano.
idea.situation-brief.lead: SKU atlas.situation.brief@v1 fuses map layers inside a bbox — flood, EFFIS, lightning, volcano, alerts, events included by default; not spacewx/geomag/argo — score, drivers, citations, receipt. Fail-closed if no LIVE coverage. Pairings are co-presence, not forecasts.
idea.situation-brief.who: Who pays: site ops, brokers, and risk agents that need a fileable brief — not another raw sensor poll.
idea.situation-brief.artifact: Artifact: versioned situation brief (score + drivers + citations[]) + sha256 receipt.
idea.situation-brief.not: Not: a forecast service, insurance adjuster, or chat without an artifact.
idea.situation-brief.hard: Hard bit: honest refuse when LIVE pins are missing; cross-layer claims must cite ids.
idea.nearest-read.title: Nearest LIVE by coordinates
idea.nearest-read.teaser: Buy atlas.nearest.read@v1 — lat/lon → nearest LIVE pin, distance_km, receipt.
idea.nearest-read.lead: What GAIA cannot sell honestly: buyer geography on fixed sensors stays operator-anchored. ATLAS indexes the map and returns the nearest LIVE pin (layer filter, max_km). Fail-closed if nothing LIVE is in range.
idea.nearest-read.who: Who pays: agents and apps that already know a site lat/lon and need one attested reading — not a device_id scavenger hunt.
idea.nearest-read.artifact: Artifact: nearest pin citation (values + distance_km + layer) + sha256 receipt; optional per_layer map.
idea.nearest-read.not: Not: a geocoder, forecast, or a substitute for GAIA device_id custody on fixed relays.
idea.nearest-read.hard: Hard bit: refuse when coverage is empty or beyond max_km — never invent a “nearby” SIM pin.
idea.gnss-jamming-alert.title: GNSS Threat Watchbox
idea.gnss-jamming-alert.teaser: Curated ACTIVE/MONITORING GNSS records → source-attributed watch events for a defined area.
idea.gnss-jamming-alert.lead: The underlying feed is a curated CC BY 4.0 incident registry relayed through GAIA and mapped by ATLAS. It is useful threat intelligence, but it is not raw RF sensing, independent confirmation, or a working alert delivery product yet.
idea.gnss-jamming-alert.who: Who pays: fleet telematics, maritime, and logistics risk ops. Aviation GNSS integrity is a real market (ADS-B products exist) — this card is not that product.
idea.gnss-jamming-alert.artifact: Artifact: source-attributed watch event with registry status, event time, severity, radius, citations, and receipt.
idea.gnss-jamming-alert.not: Not: raw spectrum measurement, independent confirmation, ATC, or guaranteed detection.
idea.gnss-jamming-alert.hard: Hard bit: validate density, freshness, false-positive policy, deduplication, and delivery with a design partner; preserve CC BY attribution and exclude resolved/historical records from the active view.
idea.gnss-jamming-alert.step1: Inspect the jamming layer in ATLAS

idea.sensor-publisher.lead: Supply path is live: map → capability → Hub. Keys, LIVE/SIM discipline, and listing are the build.
idea.sensor-publisher.hard: Hard bit: key custody, calibration, LIVE/SIM enforcement, cold-start buyers. Start on the live map — not an offline brief.

idea.parametric-trigger.not: Not: paying claims or acting as adjuster.
idea.parametric-trigger.hard: Hard bit: policy-as-data, quorum, partner adapters, dispute window.

proof.arch.label: CLICK THE SYSTEM
proof.arch.source.body: A physical sensor or declared external feed observes the world. Provenance starts here; source and time must survive every downstream step.
proof.arch.gaia.body: GAIA normalizes the reading and returns an Ed25519-signed attestation. The signature identifies the emitter; it does not by itself prove the world claim is true.
proof.arch.atlas.body: ATLAS makes source, freshness, coverage, and LIVE versus SIM mode inspectable by humans and agents.
proof.arch.hub.body: Hub exposes a named capability with a declared price and invocation contract, so an agent can buy one bounded result.
proof.arch.product.body: A focused product converts the receipt-backed input into one decision: alert, evidence pack, watchbox, or trigger.
proof.arch.metis.body: Metis is an optional reasoning verifier for generated interpretations. It does not replace source provenance or physical checks.
proof.terms.label: PLAIN-LANGUAGE DECODER
proof.term.live: A current reading from a declared external source. LIVE means non-simulated and source-attributed—not independently proven truth.
proof.term.sim: Synthetic or replayed data used for demos and testing. It remains visibly separate from LIVE.
proof.term.attestation: Signed metadata that binds a result to an emitter, sequence, and time. It supports checking provenance; it does not independently prove every claim.
proof.term.invoke: One call to a named capability with a defined input, output, and price.
proof.term.receipt: A durable record of the call, result, policy outcome, and identifiers needed for audit or dispute.
proof.term.pay: A settlement policy: usable output becomes payment-eligible; declared failure can refund and silence costs zero. It is not a guarantee that every signed fact is true.
econ.label: INTERACTIVE UNIT ECONOMICS
econ.title: See how a micro-call becomes a market.
econ.sub: Change every assumption. This is a transparent model, not a revenue forecast.
econ.note: Illustration before infrastructure, verification, support, tax, and acquisition costs. No forecast or promised return.

idea.flood-hydrology.title: Flood Hydrology Evidence
idea.flood-hydrology.teaser: Buy atlas.situation.brief@v1 on flood + river — cited US alerts and gauges, not a flood model.
idea.flood-hydrology.lead: The callable brief returns LIVE NWS CAP flood / flash-flood alerts and river-gauge pins in a bbox, names the hydrology pairing when both are present, and attaches a content receipt. Coverage is US-centric. Empty bbox refuses. This is an evidence pack for ops tickets — not Floodbase, Fathom, GloFAS, or an NFIP price.
idea.flood-hydrology.who: Who pays: US terminals, yards, and facility ops that already buy site weather desks; cat-ops rooms that need a cited nowcast adjunct rather than a quote.
idea.flood-hydrology.artifact: Artifact: situation brief (flood + river citations, hydrology pairing driver, score, receipt). Repeating path: watchbox on the same layers.
idea.flood-hydrology.not: Not: a flood model, 50-year index, parametric quote, GloFAS scrape, evacuation order, or insurance payout.
idea.flood-hydrology.hard: Hard bit: CAP coverage is the US plus the UK Environment Agency (England only — not SEPA/NRW); WaterWatch JSON is retired; pairing is co-presence, not a hydrologic forecast; extra ECCC/SMHI river pins do not make a global flood model; never pad empty basins with SIM.
idea.flood-hydrology.step3: Discover the paid brief on Hub
idea.nordic-ais.title: Nordic Public AIS Snapshot
idea.nordic-ais.teaser: Buy gaia.ais.public.read@v1 — Finnish and Norwegian public AIS, two licences, not global AIS.
idea.nordic-ais.lead: The Hub SKU relays two national public AIS networks: Fintraffic Digitraffic (Finnish waters, CC BY 4.0) and Kystverket via BarentsWatch (Norwegian waters, NLOD 2.0). Every reading declares the credit its own licence requires, so the artifact carries its own attribution. ATLAS fans vessels onto the public AIS layer for the analyst and watchboxes. It is not GFW, not AISStream, and not own-edge gaia.ais.read@v1 (your receiver).
idea.nordic-ais.who: Who pays: Baltic, Gulf-of-Finland and Norwegian-coast maritime ops and port desks that already need a cited vessel picture — not a global fishing or dark-fleet product.
idea.nordic-ais.artifact: Artifact: attested AIS cluster (SOG/COG/lat/lon + MMSI list) and ATLAS pins. Repeating path: watchbox on layer ais.
idea.nordic-ais.not: Not: own-edge AIS, GFW, global coverage, one fused Nordic picture, or an identity/sanctions product.
idea.nordic-ais.hard: Hard bit: two sources, two licences — carry the attribution the reading itself declares (CC BY 4.0 credit Fintraffic; NLOD 2.0 credit Kystverket/BarentsWatch), never one fixed credit; the Norwegian feed omits fishing vessels under 15 m and leisure under 45 m; coverage stops at those two national networks; do not silently merge with feeder-ais-01.
idea.nordic-ais.step2: Inspect the GAIA public AIS SKU
idea.nordic-ais.step3: Discover the paid capability on Hub
idea.tsunami-cap.title: Tsunami CAP Watch
idea.tsunami-cap.teaser: NWS CAP and PTWC tsunami bulletins on ATLAS — often empty, never a tide gauge.
idea.tsunami-cap.lead: gaia.tsunami.read@v1 relays NWS CAP tsunami products (U.S. PD) and PTWC Atom bulletins (Pacific). Empty feed is offline and must not debit. These are warning products, not a tide gauge or a tsunami sensor. Quiet days are the honest default.
idea.tsunami-cap.who: Who pays: Pacific / US coastal ops desks that already consume NWS CAP and need a cited empty-or-live pin they can attach to a ticket.
idea.tsunami-cap.artifact: Artifact: CAP cluster when alerts exist; otherwise a fail-closed offline. Repeating path: watchbox on layer tsunami.
idea.tsunami-cap.not: Not: a tide gauge, DART buoy, inundation model, evacuation order, or a guaranteed detection.
idea.tsunami-cap.hard: Hard bit: two issuing centres behind one SKU — the reading names which one; the feed is quiet most days; product value is fail-closed silence plus a watchbox, not a fake tsunami heatmap.
idea.campus-nowcast.title: Campus Physical Nowcast
idea.campus-nowcast.teaser: One campus bbox → default-layer situation brief (fire, flood, alerts, weather, jamming when LIVE).
idea.campus-nowcast.lead: Colo and hyperscaler campuses already buy 30-year climate siting. This SKU is the other job: a fileable LIVE nowcast over the fence line. atlas.situation.brief@v1 defaults to map layers. Fail-closed if nothing LIVE is in the bbox. First Street / XDI remain the siting products — we do not replace them.
idea.campus-nowcast.who: Who pays: data-center NOC and campus facilities teams that need an ops snapshot they can attach to a ticket, not a 30-year hazard percentile.
idea.campus-nowcast.artifact: Artifact: situation brief for a named campus bbox (drivers + citations[] + receipt).
idea.campus-nowcast.not: Not: climate-scenario software, insurability certificate, Schneider ClimVaR, or guaranteed coverage of every hazard.
idea.campus-nowcast.hard: Hard bit: named-site registry, poll cadence, ticket attach, and honest refuse when the campus bbox is sparse — that application layer is what you still build.
idea.campus-nowcast.step2: POST situation-brief for the campus bbox
idea.cyclone-watch.title: Named-Storm Watch
idea.cyclone-watch.teaser: Buy gaia.cyclone.read@v1 — the current NHC advisory position, signed. Not a forecast track.
idea.cyclone-watch.lead: NOAA NHC and CPHC publish active storms; this SKU relays the current advisory — position, intensity in knots, central pressure — as an Ed25519-attested reading (U.S. public domain). ATLAS pins it on the cyclone layer so a watchbox can fire when a named storm enters your bbox. Off-season the feed is empty, which is offline and must not debit.
idea.cyclone-watch.who: Who pays: Gulf and Atlantic terminal, port and offshore-logistics desks that already read NHC advisories but need a signed, timestamped artifact to attach to a closure or sailing decision.
idea.cyclone-watch.artifact: Artifact: attested storm cluster (name, classification, storm id, intensity, pressure, position) plus ATLAS pins. Repeating path: watchbox on layer cyclone.
idea.cyclone-watch.not: Not: a forecast track, a cone of uncertainty, a JTWC feed, a NW-Pacific typhoon product, a parametric trigger, or an evacuation order.
idea.cyclone-watch.hard: Hard bit: this is the position NHC has already published, not a model run — it trails the storm, never leads it; coverage is Atlantic, East Pacific and Central Pacific only, so a Western-Pacific typhoon is simply absent rather than late; most of the year the honest answer is an empty feed.
idea.cyclone-watch.step3: Discover the paid capability on Hub
idea.adsb-overflight.title: Overflight Log (anchored)
idea.adsb-overflight.teaser: ADSB.lol aircraft around one operator anchor. Honest today: you cannot yet point it at your own site.
idea.adsb-overflight.lead: gaia.adsb.public.read@v1 relays an ADSB.lol area snapshot — position, altitude, ground speed, ICAO address, callsign — around a single anchor fixed by the operator, under ODbL 1.0. It is not own-edge gaia.adsb.read@v1 (your receiver), not OpenSky and not ADSBx. Published as a hypothesis, not a wedge: the product a buyer would want is not yet the product that exists.
idea.adsb-overflight.who: Who pays: nobody yet, honestly. The shape it would fit is a site-security or noise-complaint desk that needs a cited overflight record — but only once the anchor is theirs to choose.
idea.adsb-overflight.artifact: Artifact: attested aircraft cluster around the operator anchor plus ATLAS pins. The repeating path would be a watchbox on layer adsb.
idea.adsb-overflight.not: Not: own-edge ADS-B, OpenSky, ADSBx, global coverage, a per-site anchor, a tracking or identity product, or anything airspace-authoritative.
idea.adsb-overflight.hard: Hard bit — two blockers, both real: the capability takes only a device_id, so the anchor is whatever the operator deployed and a buyer cannot pass their own coordinates; and ODbL 1.0 is share-alike, so any derived public database must be released under ODbL too — fine for a receipt attached to a ticket, contagious for a product database. Per-call coordinates and a licence review are what would turn this into a wedge.

idea.geomag-window.title: Geomagnetic Operations Window
idea.geomag-window.teaser: One coordinate → planetary Kp in NOAA's own states, plus the nearest USGS observatory. atlas.geomag.window@v1, $0.05.
idea.geomag-window.lead: The cross-layer brief deliberately excludes spacewx and geomag — a planetary index is not a site brief — so the two densest new layers had no SKU at all: 401 SWPC observations and 13 of 14 USGS observatories LIVE, unsold. This one answers the question desks actually pay for: is the field quiet enough to run the operation now.
idea.geomag-window.who: Who pays: directional-drilling and MWD survey desks that already pause survey acceptance during disturbance; HF radio and polar-route operators; RTK and geodetic crews watching ionospheric scintillation.
idea.geomag-window.artifact: Artifact: Kp with the NOAA state and G-scale, a window status of open / caution / hold, the nearest LIVE observatory with distance, total field F and observation age, the nearest OVATION aurora cell, and a signed receipt.
idea.geomag-window.not: Not: a magnetic-declination correction, an IFR-grade in-field reference, a local variometer, or a safety-of-life service.
idea.geomag-window.hard: Hard bit: the USGS network is United States territory, so anywhere else the answer is planetary-only and has to say so — the payload carries corroboration: planetary_only rather than implying a magnetometer nobody has. No LIVE Kp is a refusal, not a window derived from an observatory alone.
idea.pv-irradiance-record.title: PV Irradiance Record of Fact
idea.pv-irradiance-record.teaser: Plant coordinate → dated all-sky vs clear-sky irradiation with aerosol and dust. atlas.pv.irradiance.record@v1, $0.15.
idea.pv-irradiance-record.lead: NASA POWER publishes daily irradiation with a multi-day lag. That makes it useless as a nowcast and exactly right for the argument this SKU serves: what the sky and the air actually did over one plant coordinate on the day in dispute, signed and dated.
idea.pv-irradiance-record.who: Who pays: PV owners, asset managers and independent engineers arguing performance ratio with an EPC or O&M contractor, plus warranty claim handlers. The question they buy is one sentence: was the underperformance the weather and the dust, or the contractor?
idea.pv-irradiance-record.artifact: Artifact: the POWER record date, all-sky and clear-sky kWh/m²/day with the derived cloud loss, colocated CAMS aerosol optical depth and dust, and the nearest weather pin — every one with its distance from the plant — plus a signed receipt.
idea.pv-irradiance-record.not: Not: a yield forecast, a soiling-loss model, a bankable energy assessment — no P50/P90 and no uncertainty band — or a pyranometer on the plant.
idea.pv-irradiance-record.hard: Hard bit: POWER and CAMS are global services, but ATLAS pins configured coordinates, so onboarding a customer plant means adding its coordinate to the operator's sensor config. Beyond max_km the SKU refuses instead of issuing a record of fact from a grid cell on another continent.
idea.pv-irradiance-record.step1: Open the solar and aerosol layers
idea.smoke-operations.title: Asset Smoke Containment Brief
idea.smoke-operations.teaser: Is this exact asset inside a NOAA HMS smoke polygon? atlas.smoke.operations@v1, $0.12 — point-in-polygon, not centroid distance.
idea.smoke-operations.lead: Exact point-in-polygon against the complete Ed25519-bound HMS geometry inventory, fused with PM2.5 and AQI at the same coordinate. HMS writes one dated analysis per UTC day, so the brief names the analysis date it read rather than implying a live satellite pass.
idea.smoke-operations.who: Who pays: film and television production insurers, outdoor construction and mining, ports, school districts — and anyone enforcing an AQI threshold written into a contract or a labour rule, which is where willingness to pay is strongest.
idea.smoke-operations.artifact: Artifact: the containment verdict with each covering polygon and its signed geometry digest, colocated PM2.5/AQI, an operational status, the HMS analysis date and its age, and a signed receipt.
idea.smoke-operations.not: Not: measured PM2.5 at the asset, an evacuation order, a medical opinion, or a live satellite pass.
idea.smoke-operations.hard: Hard bit: the current UTC day's HMS product does not exist until the first daytime analysis — at 06:00Z it simply 404s — so the read walks back one dated product at a time and carries the date through to the answer. A truncated polygon inventory is refused rather than decided against part of itself.

idea.desk-presets.title: Named Desks on One Brief
idea.desk-presets.teaser: port_desk · corridor · cat_desk — a fixed layer set and a stated scope on atlas.situation.brief@v1, $0.06.
idea.desk-presets.lead: Every paid invoke this hub has recorded went to the cross-layer situation brief. Yet a buyer who wanted a berth-window answer had to already know which of 39 layers to ask for. A preset is the job title: it fixes the layers, states what the answer is valid for, and refuses a misspelled desk instead of quietly selling the 21-layer default.
idea.desk-presets.who: Who pays: port and terminal duty desks, rail and road corridor control rooms, and catastrophe desks that need a territory digest they can file. The same rail, sold as a seat rather than a call.
idea.desk-presets.artifact: Artifact: the brief carrying preset, preset_scope and the fixed layer list — and over an empty bbox, a refusal that still names the desk and shows per-layer coverage. A watchbox turns the same call into a repeating signed delivery.
idea.desk-presets.not: Not: a forecast, an insurance trigger, a port closure order, a pilotage decision, a track-level inspection, or a loss estimate.
idea.desk-presets.hard: Hard bit: an explicit layers list overrides the preset, and then the scope sentence no longer describes the answer — so the payload reports preset_overridden instead of echoing a desk that did not shape the brief. Self-serve subscriptions are still off until the operator opens watchbox signup.

idea.route-integrity.title: Route Integrity Brief
idea.route-integrity.teaser: A polyline corridor → per-segment GNSS coverage, reported interference, platform presence and hazard pins. atlas.route.integrity@v1, $0.25.
idea.route-integrity.lead: The GNSS SKU already accepted a route and almost nobody used it — one observation in thirty days — because a degradation field on its own is not a decision. This composes it with the curated interference registry, the AIS and ADS-B platforms that happen to be in the same corridor, and the hazard pins beside it, attributed to the leg they sit on.
idea.route-integrity.who: Who pays: marine P&I and hull underwriters and charterers, for whom GNSS interference in the Baltic and Black Sea is already a rated risk; BVLOS drone operators who owe a regulator an evidence file; survey and geodetic contractors.
idea.route-integrity.artifact: Artifact: per-segment counts with length, the GNSS field in route mode, the reported zones the corridor intersects with their claim class, AIS/ADS-B presence counts, hazard pins with distances, an integrity_claim of reported_interference / station_coverage_only / no_gnss_coverage, and a signed receipt.
idea.route-integrity.not: Not: proof of jamming or spoofing, a spectrum measurement, a safety-of-life navigation service, a routing instruction, or a clearance.
idea.route-integrity.hard: Hard bit: the honest measurement is unflattering — the station layer reports zero stations transmitting now and four hundred unknown coverage cells, so today this is reported zones plus a station inventory, not live integrity. The strong version needs an operator account at EarthScope or MIRAI, both already licence-approved.
idea.route-integrity.step1: Open the GNSS and interference layers
idea.observability-attest.title: Data-Availability Attestation
idea.observability-attest.teaser: Not what the weather was — what data existed, and whether the instrument was up. atlas.observability.attest@v1, $0.10.
idea.observability-attest.lead: A NEXRAD outage is a routine reason a weather-dependent claim gets contested, and until now ATLAS could only answer for right now. An append-only status archive makes the past answerable: the nearest radars, their archived status samples inside the window, and the extent of the archive itself.
idea.observability-attest.who: Who pays: crop and property claim adjusters, litigation support, and parametric underwriters whose contract says "per the nearest radar" and who need to show what the nearest radar was doing.
idea.observability-attest.artifact: Artifact: the radars in range with distance, current status and their archived samples in the window; window_coverage of none / partial / recorded with the archive's own start and end; active CAP alerts; and a signed receipt.
idea.observability-attest.not: Not: reflectivity, a weather reconstruction, an adjudication of the claim, or anything outside United States territory.
idea.observability-attest.hard: Hard bit: the whole product rests on one distinction that is easy to lose — a recorded degraded status is evidence the radar was impaired, while a gap in our sampling is evidence of nothing. The payload keeps them apart, and a window older than the archive is reported as uncovered rather than clean.
